skill.name: azure-communication-callautomation-java
skill.description: Build Java call automation workflows with Azure Communication Services. Use it for IVR, call routing, call recording, DTMF, speech, and text-to-speech.
skill.summary: Guides Java developers through Azure Communication Services Call Automation patterns.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static command, network, and reconnaissance findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples, SDK placeholders, and Java sample code. No prompt injection, hidden executable behavior, or unauthorized network destination was found. The remaining concerns are privacy risks around logging DTMF input and handling call recordings.

remediation.issue: DTMF input may contain account numbers or other sensitive caller data.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid printing DTMF tones or speech results, and document redaction before data reaches logs.

remediation.issue: Recording examples do not describe consent, retention, or secure storage controls.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to obtain consent, restrict recording access, encrypt storage, and define retention periods.

content.user_title: Build Azure Call Automation Java Workflows
content.value_statement: Call automation code often requires many SDK objects, webhook events, and media options. This skill gives Java-focused examples for IVR, routing, recording, speech, and DTMF workflows.
actual_capabilities: Adds the Azure Communication Services Call Automation Maven dependency.
Creates clients with DefaultAzureCredential or a connection string.
Creates outbound calls and answers incoming Event Grid calls.
Plays text-to-speech prompts and audio files during calls.
Recognizes DTMF tones and speech with timeout settings.
Starts recordings, manages participants, transfers calls, and handles webhook events.
limitations: Requires an Azure Communication Services resource and valid authentication.
Provides examples, not a complete production webhook service.
Uses placeholder phone numbers, URLs, and identifiers that must be replaced.
Does not implement consent, retention, or access controls for call recordings.

use_cases.title: Create IVR Menus
use_cases.description: Build Java call flows that greet callers, play prompts, and route DTMF choices.

use_cases.title: Automate Contact Center Calls
use_cases.description: Answer incoming calls, add participants, transfer callers, and respond to webhook events.

use_cases.title: Prototype Voice Experiences
use_cases.description: Test speech recognition, text-to-speech prompts, recordings, and error handling before production work.

prompt_templates.title: Add the SDK
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add Azure Communication Services Call Automation to a Java Maven project and create the client.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Outbound Call
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to create an outbound ACS call in Java with a callback URL and caller ID.

prompt_templates.title: Build a DTMF IVR
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Java IVR flow that plays a prompt, collects DTMF input, and routes the caller.

prompt_templates.title: Design Event Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a robust ACS Call Automation webhook handler with recording, transfer, error handling, and privacy safeguards.

output_examples.input: I need an IVR that routes callers to sales or support.
output: A text-to-speech greeting and DTMF recognition step.
Routing logic for sales, support, invalid input, and timeout cases.

output_examples.input: I want to answer incoming calls from Event Grid.
output: Event parsing for connected, recognized, playback, and disconnected states.

output_examples.input: I need guidance for recording a call safely.
output: Recording start, pause, resume, stop, and download steps.
A note to avoid logging recording URLs or caller input.

best_practices: Store endpoints, callback URLs, and connection strings in managed configuration.
Validate webhook requests and handle retries, duplicate events, and failed media operations.
Mask caller input, protect recordings, and document consent and retention rules.
anti_patterns: Using sample phone numbers, callback URLs, or resource names unchanged.
Logging DTMF tones, speech text, recording URLs, or connection strings.
Building call flows without timeout paths, validation, or error handling.

faq.question: What Azure service does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Azure Communication Services Call Automation for Java applications.

faq.question: Can it help build an IVR system?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes prompt playback, DTMF recognition, speech recognition, and call routing examples.

faq.question: Does it include authentication examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows DefaultAzureCredential and connection string client creation patterns.

faq.question: Does it create a full server application?
faq.answer: No. It provides focused SDK examples and webhook handling patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with call recording?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows starting, pausing, resuming, stopping, and downloading recordings.

faq.question: What should teams secure before production use?
faq.answer: Teams should secure webhooks, secrets, callback URLs, recordings, logs, and caller input.
